Participant Flow.Recruitment Details
segments.en_txt: All participants had established type 2 diabetes and were recruited from 77 clinical centers in the United States (64 sites) and Canada (13 sites). Recruitment occurred in two phases, from January to June 2001 and from February 2003 to October 2005.

segments.path: Participant Flow.Pre-assignment Details
segments.en_txt: Eligible participants provided evidence of ability to routinely monitor capillary blood sugars from written records or electronic downloads from a self-monitoring blood glucose device (SMBG), or (in cases where such records could not be provided) underwent a 2 to 4-week pre-randomization run-in period to evaluate compliance with SMBG monitoring.

segments.path: Participant Flow.Arm/Group Description.Glycemia Trial: Intensive Control/BP Trial: Intensive Control
segments.en_txt:
Glycemia Trial - Open label administration of oral anti-hyperglycemic agents and/or insulin in combination with dietary/lifestyle advice as needed to achieve glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels \<6.0%. Anti-hyperglycemic agents include multiple drugs including insulins and oral anti-hyperglycemic agents as needed to reach Glycemia Trial arm-specific goals.

BP Trial - Open label administration of anti-hypertensive agents to reduce and maintain systolic blood pressure (SBP) level to \<120 mmHg. Anti-hypertensive agents include multiple anti-hypertensive medications as needed to reach Blood Pressure Trial arm-specific goals.

segments.path: Participant Flow.Arm/Group Description.Glycemia Trial: Intensive Control/BP Trial: Standard Control
segments.en_txt:
Glycemia Trial - Open label administration of oral anti-hyperglycemic agents and/or insulin in combination with dietary/lifestyle advice as needed to achieve glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels \<6.0%. Anti-hyperglycemic agents include multiple drugs including insulins and oral anti-hyperglycemic agents as needed to reach Glycemia Trial arm-specific goals.

BP Trial - Open label administration of multiple anti-hypertensive agents to maintain SBP level \<140 mm Hg. Anti-hypertensive agents include multiple anti-hypertensive medications as needed to reach Blood Pressure Trial arm-specific goals.

segments.path: Participant Flow.Arm/Group Description.Glycemia Trial: Intensive Control/Lipid Trial: Fenofibrate
segments.en_txt:
Glycemia Trial - Open label administration of oral anti-hyperglycemic agents and/or insulin in combination with dietary/lifestyle advice as needed to achieve glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels \<6.0%. Anti-hyperglycemic agents include multiple drugs including insulins and oral anti-hyperglycemic agents as needed to reach Glycemia Trial arm-specific goals.

Lipid Trial - Double blind administration of 160 mg/day of fenofibrate in participants with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥50 mL/min/1.73m\^2 or 54 mg/day in patients with eGFR \<50 mL/min/1.73m\^2 in combination with open label simvastatin. Blinded fenofibrate or placebo plus simvastatin includes double blind administration of 160 mg/day of fenofibrate in participants with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥50 mL/min/1.73m\^2 or 54 mg/day in patients with eGFR \<50 mL/min/1.73m\^2 or matching placebo in combination with open label simvastatin 20 - 40 mg/day.

segments.path: Participant Flow.Arm/Group Description.Glycemia Trial: Intensive Control/Lipid Trial: Placebo
segments.en_txt:

Double blind administration of placebo matching either 160 mg/day in participants with eGFR ≥50 mL/min/1.73m2 or 54 mg/day in participants with eGFR \<50 mL/min/1.73m\^2 in combination with open label simvastatin. Blinded fenofibrate or placebo plus simvastatin includes double blind administration of 160 mg/day of fenofibrate in participants with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥50 mL/min/1.73m\^2 or 54 mg/day in patients with eGFR \<50 mL/min/1.73m\^2 or matching placebo in combination with open label simvastatin 20 - 40 mg/day.

segments.en_txt: First Occurrence of a Major Cardiovascular Event (MCE); Specifically Nonfatal Heart Attack, Nonfatal Stroke, or Cardiovascular Death (Measured Throughout the Study) in the Glycemia Trial.

segments.path: Outcome Measures[0].Description
segments.en_txt:
Time to first occurrence of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or cardiovascular death. This was the primary outcome measure in all three trials: Glycemia (all participants), Blood Pressure (subgroup of participants not in Lipid Trial), and Lipid (subgroup of participants not in Blood Pressure Trial).

In the Glycemia Trial, a finding of higher mortality in the intensive arm group led to an early discontinuation of therapy after a mean of 3.5 years of follow-up. Intensive arm participants were transitioned to standard arm strategy over a period of 0.2 year and followed for an additional 1.2 years to the planned end of the Glycemia Trial while participating in one of the other sub-trials (BP or Lipid) to their planned completion.

Outcome Measures[0].Analysis Population Description
segments.en_txt: The population analyzed included all participants randomized and was performed by intention to treat with right-censoring of participants who did not complete follow-up prior to occurrence of MCE.

Outcome Measures[1].Arm/Group Description.Glycemia Trial: Intensive Control
segments.en_txt: Open label administration of oral anti-hyperglycemic agents and/or insulin in combination with dietary/lifestyle advice as needed to achieve glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels \<6.0%. Anti-hyperglycemic agents include multiple drugs including insulins and oral anti-hyperglycemic agents as needed to reach Glycemia Trial arm-specific goals.

segments.path: Outcome Measures[1].Arm/Group Description.Glycemia Trial: Standard Control
segments.en_txt: Open label administration of oral anti-hyperglycemic agents and/or insulin in combination with dietary/lifestyle advice as needed to achieve glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels of 7.0 to 7.9%. Anti-hyperglycemic agents include multiple drugs including insulins and oral anti-hyperglycemic agents as needed to reach Glycemia Trial arm-specific goals.

Outcome Measures[2].Analysis Population Description

Outcome Measures[4].Arm/Group Description.Lipid Trial: Fenofibrate
segments.en_txt: Double blind administration of 160 mg/day of fenofibrate in participants with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥50 mL/min/1.73m\^2 or 54 mg/day in patients with eGFR \<50 mL/min/1.73m\^2, in combination with open label simvastatin 20 - 40 mg/day.

segments.en_txt: Double blind administration of placebo matching either 160 mg/day in participants with eGFR ≥50 mL/min/1.73m\^2 or 54 mg/day in participants with eGFR \<50 mL/min/1.73m\^2, in combination with open label simvastatin 20 - 40 mg/day.

Adverse Events.Time Frame
segments.en_txt: Includes Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) reported after randomization and throughout the planned observation period, mean follow-up was 4.9 years. Data on other (non-serious) adverse events were not collected.

segments.path: Adverse Events.Adverse Event Reporting Description
segments.en_txt: SAEs were defined as any adverse experience that was significantly life threatening and/or resulted in death, permanent disability, hospitalization or prolongation of hospitalization, myositis/myopathy, or hepatitis and were considered by the investigators to be possibly, probably, or definitely related to study treatments.
